title: Vibration survey before pulling a critical gearbox
decision: Pull the gearbox for overhaul now, or leave it in service
theta_definition: theta=1: an incipient bearing fault is present in the gearbox

p.reasoning: Critical gearboxes are monitored and usually healthy; incipient faults at any given inspection are uncommon but not rare on aging fleets.

s.reasoning: Vibration analysis catches most developed bearing faults but can miss early-stage or low-signal faults.

t.reasoning: False alarms from misalignment or noise happen but competent analysts keep them modest.

e.reasoning: Reliability engineers usually act on a credible fault call and planned overhaul usually prevents the failure.

B.reasoning: Avoided unplanned failure (secondary damage, downtime) minus the planned repair cost; heavy tail for production-critical trains.

K.reasoning: Unnecessary teardown plus scheduled downtime for a healthy gearbox.

C.reasoning: A single third-party vibration survey visit and report.

title: Pre-employment ergonomic screening before hiring a warehouse worker
decision: Reject or modify duties for the applicant, or hire as normal
theta_definition: theta=1: the applicant is at high musculoskeletal injury risk in this role

p.reasoning: A minority of warehouse applicants carry elevated injury risk for heavy lifting roles.

s.reasoning: Functional screens are mediocre predictors of future injury; predictive validity studies show modest sensitivity.

t.reasoning: Screens flag a nontrivial share of applicants who would have been fine.

e.reasoning: Managers often act on a failed screen, but rejecting one applicant only partially prevents injuries (replacement risk, imperfect prevention).

B.reasoning: An avoided lost-time musculoskeletal claim: typical workers-compensation claim tens of thousands USD, tail to serious back injury.

K.reasoning: Wrongly rejecting a good candidate: re-recruiting, vacancy time, possible discrimination exposure.

C.reasoning: Commercial pre-employment functional screening per applicant.

title: Dangerous-capability evaluation of a frontier AI model before deployment
decision: Delay deployment and add mitigations, or deploy on schedule
theta_definition: theta=1: the model materially uplifts biological misuse capability

p.reasoning: For a frontier model at current capability margins, material bio uplift is plausible but not the default expectation.

s.reasoning: Evals can miss capabilities via under-elicitation; sensitivity is real but far from assured.

t.reasoning: A careful eval rarely claims uplift where there is none, but threshold judgments are noisy.

e.reasoning: Labs do gate deployments on eval results and mitigations mostly work once the risk is flagged.

B.reasoning: Avoided expected harm, liability and trust damage from deploying an uplifting model; catastrophic tail dominates.

K.reasoning: Unneeded launch delay, mitigation engineering and lost revenue when the model was actually safe.

title: Standardized manipulation benchmark of a warehouse robot before a fleet purchase
decision: Walk away or renegotiate the fleet purchase, or buy as planned
theta_definition: theta=1: the robot underperforms its spec in the buyer's actual workflow
instrument: One standardized manipulation benchmark campaign on the buyer's item mix

p.reasoning: Vendor demos overstate in-situ performance often; underperformance vs spec in a specific workflow is common.

s.reasoning: A benchmark on the buyer's own item mix usually exposes real shortfalls.

t.reasoning: Benchmark conditions can unfairly penalize a robot that would do fine in production.

e.reasoning: Buyers act on bad benchmark results and walking away fully avoids the bad purchase.

B.reasoning: Avoided cost of a misfitting fleet: integration rework, throughput shortfall, partial write-off on a multi-robot order.

K.reasoning: Walking away from a good deal: sourcing delay, price premium on the alternative.

C.reasoning: A benchmark campaign with the vendor's robot on representative items.

title: Soil pathogen assay before planting a high-value crop
decision: Fumigate/rotate/switch fields, or plant as planned
theta_definition: theta=1: soil pathogen load is high enough to threaten the crop
instrument: One laboratory soil pathogen assay panel

p.reasoning: Fields chosen for high-value crops are usually vetted; serious pathogen load present a minority of the time.

s.reasoning: Lab assays detect most economically relevant loads but sampling can miss patchy infestations.

t.reasoning: Detection thresholds are conservative; some positives are agronomically irrelevant.

e.reasoning: Operators usually act on a positive assay; fumigation or switching mostly prevents the loss.

B.reasoning: Avoided loss of a high-value crop stand on the affected acreage (e.g. berries or vegetables).

K.reasoning: Unneeded fumigation cost or forgone margin from switching away from the best crop.

C.reasoning: A soil sampling round plus a laboratory pathogen panel.

title: Structural inspection before purchasing a used mobile crane
decision: Walk away or renegotiate, or buy the crane as offered
theta_definition: theta=1: the crane has disqualifying structural damage or fatigue cracking
instrument: One third-party structural inspection with NDT (non-destructive testing)

p.reasoning: Used cranes on the secondary market frequently hide structural issues, though most units are serviceable.

s.reasoning: NDT by a competent inspector finds most disqualifying cracks and repairs.

t.reasoning: Some cosmetic findings are wrongly escalated to disqualifying.

e.reasoning: A buyer who paid for the inspection almost always acts on a bad report, and walking away avoids the loss.

B.reasoning: Avoided bad purchase: repair or write-off of a compromised crane, plus liability exposure from a structural failure.

K.reasoning: Losing a good deal: re-sourcing time and price premium on the next crane.

C.reasoning: A third-party structural inspection with NDT on a mobile crane.

title: Sepsis-risk panel for a newly admitted patient
decision: Start the sepsis bundle (cultures, early antibiotics, monitoring), or standard care
theta_definition: theta=1: early sepsis is present at admission

p.reasoning: Among general admissions without obvious sepsis, early sepsis is present in a small fraction.

s.reasoning: Biomarker panels catch most early sepsis but miss atypical presentations.

t.reasoning: Inflammation from other causes produces false positives at a meaningful rate.

e.reasoning: Physicians act on a positive panel and early bundles substantially reduce mortality and ICU escalation.

B.reasoning: Avoided mortality risk and ICU escalation from earlier treatment; a few percent mortality reduction against a statistical-life-scale loss, plus avoided ICU cost.

K.reasoning: Unnecessary broad-spectrum antibiotics, extra monitoring, longer stay, antimicrobial-resistance externality per decision.

C.reasoning: One biomarker panel including lab handling.

title: Counterparty credit report before extending 90-day trade credit
decision: Require prepayment or decline terms, or extend 90-day credit
theta_definition: theta=1: the counterparty will default within the credit terms

p.reasoning: Trade-credit default rates for screened B2B counterparties run low single digits.

s.reasoning: Credit reports flag many but far from all imminent defaults; fresh distress is often missed.

t.reasoning: Healthy firms occasionally screen badly on stale or thin files.

e.reasoning: A CFO who ordered the report acts on it, and requiring prepayment directly eliminates the exposure.

B.reasoning: Avoided write-off of the receivable on a typical order.

K.reasoning: Lost sale margin or soured relationship from demanding prepayment of a good customer.

C.reasoning: One commercial credit report with analyst notes.
